sentences.text: Sulcavis is a monotypic extinct genus of enantiornithean birds, a diverse group of early avians that lived in what is now China during the Early Cretaceous.
This genus differs from other Enantiornithes by possessing enlarged teeth with grooves on their inner surface, a feature that gives the genus its name.
These robust teeth contained internal grooves that likely helped the animals withstand harder food items.
Sulcavis holds the distinction of being the first bird species discovered to have ornamented tooth enamel.
The genus was formally described on January 9, 2013, by a team including Jingmai Kathleen O'Connor and colleagues.
The holotype specimen was discovered near the town of Lamadong in Liaoning Province, China, within the Yixian Formation as part of the Jehol Biota.
This specific fossil was later prepared by Maureen Walsh at the Natural History Museum of Los Angeles County.
The species name 'geeorum' honors the Gee family for their contributions to Mesozoic bird research.
The genus name Sulcavis combines the Latin words for 'groove' and 'bird' to reflect its unique dental features.
Taxonomically, Sulcavis is part of the parent group Bohaiornithidae.
Current research suggests that the closest relative to Sulcavis is the genus Shenqiornis.
Fossils of this bird were found in rocks dated between 121 and 125 million years ago.
The estimated time range for Sulcavis spans from 121.4 to 113.2 million years ago.
